sentences.text: Stolokrosuchus is known from a nearly complete skull featuring a narrow, highly elongated, and tubular snout that resembles modern gharials.
The skull preserves a small, slit-like antorbital fenestra, an opening primarily formed by the lacrimal bone.
It lacks the subtympanic foramen, a feature shared with modern gharials and Pepesuchus but absent in other living crocodilians.
The quadrate bone possesses two elongated crests, labeled A and B, which served as attachment points for adductor muscles.
Its lower jaw joint was narrow and flattened, formed by dentary and splenial bones meeting at a V-shaped suture.
The splenial bone contributed approximately 25% to 30% of the total width of the lower jaw ramus.
Unlike most peirosaurids, the top surface of the lower jaw was straight instead of having a wavy profile.
Stolokrosuchus was described by Larsson and Gado in 2000.
Fossils have been found in the Lower Cretaceous Elrhaz Formation in Niger.
The fossils come from the GAD 5 site in the Aptian to Albian Elrhaz Formation in Niger.
The only known fossils were found in the Elrhaz Formation in present-day Niger.
There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Stolokrosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
Stolokrosuchus is considered semi-aquatic due to its long, tubular snout and eyes positioned on the top of its head.
Researchers suggest that Stolokrosuchus likely fed on agile prey like fish using its long and narrow jaws.
Larsson and Gado originally classified Stolokrosuchus as a peirosaurid closely related to Peirosaurus and Lomasuchus.
A 2014 study by Sertich and colleagues placed Stolokrosuchus within Peirosauridae as a derived member related to African forms like Rukwasuchus and Hamadasuchus.
A 2012 study by Bronzati and colleagues found Stolokrosuchus closely related to peirosaurids, mahajangasuchids, and Trematochampsidae, but placed this group outside Notosuchia as basal to Neosuchia.
Pinheiro and colleagues in 2023 included Stolokrosuchus within the family Itasuchidae as the most basal member.
France de Lapparent de Broin classified Stolokrosuchus in the family Elosuchidae in 2002 based on features hypothesized to be shared with Elosuchus.
Stolokrosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Stolokrosuchus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
While some studies place Stolokrosuchus within the Notosuchia, others propose a closer relationship to Neosuchia.
Some researchers suggest that Stolokrosuchus may belong to families other than Peirosauridae within Notosuchia.
Sertich and colleagues in 2014 argued that previous classifications placing Stolokrosuchus as a neosuchian might be due to missing holotype material and convergent evolution of its skull shape.
